title: Valid Palindrome
prompt: Given a string `s`, determine whether it is a palindrome after converting all uppercase letters to lowercase and removing all non-alphanumeric characters. Return `True` if it reads the same forward and backward under those rules, or `False` otherwise. An empty string (after filtering) is considered a valid palindrome.

examples.input: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"
examples.explanation: After filtering: "amanaplanacanalpanama", which is a palindrome.
After filtering: "raceacar", which is not a palindrome.
After removing the space, the string is empty, which is considered a palindrome.

constraints: s consists only of printable ASCII characters
hints: You don't need to build a separate cleaned string first — you can skip irrelevant characters on the fly while comparing.
Use two pointers starting at each end of the string, moving inward. Skip over any character that isn't a letter or digit.
When both pointers land on alphanumeric characters, compare them case-insensitively. If they ever differ, it's not a palindrome; if the pointers cross without a mismatch, it is.

solution.approach: Use two pointers, one starting at the beginning and one at the end of the string. Advance the left pointer forward and the right pointer backward whenever they land on a non-alphanumeric character. Once both point to alphanumeric characters, compare them case-insensitively; if they differ, the string isn't a palindrome. Continue until the pointers meet or cross.

input: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama
Was it a car or a cat I saw?
